answer: One workable design: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because beacon only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, umber is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any grove approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
